title: Quasi-coherent modules and maps extend across a quasi-compact open immersion
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme whose inclusion $j:U\to X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], i.e. $U\cap W$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] for every affine open $W\subseteq X$. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M$ write $\mathcal M|_U$ for its restriction to $U$ ($\mathcal M|_U(W)=\mathcal M(W)$ for opens $W\subseteq U$). Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module and let $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F|_U$ be an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map. Then there exist a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal H$, an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\psi:\mathcal H\to\mathcal F$ and an $\mathcal O_U$-linear isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal H|_U\to\mathcal G$ such that $\varphi\circ\alpha=\psi|_U$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PE (lemma-extend-trivial), part (3), lines 2787-2836 with its proof ($\mathcal H=\Ker(\mathcal F\oplus j_*\mathcal G\to j_*j^*\mathcal F)$)

proof.text: *Step 1 ($j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated).* $j$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis, i.e. in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] ($j^{-1}(W)=U\cap W$ is quasi-compact for every affine open $W\subseteq X$). $j$ is the inclusion of an open subscheme, hence an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], hence a monomorphism of schemes [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism] (the source quotes Schemes 01L7: an immersion is a monomorphism, in particular separated). So its diagonal $\Delta_j:U\to U\times_XU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is an isomorphism: the two projections $p_1,p_2:U\times_XU\to U$ satisfy $j\circ p_1=j\circ p_2$, hence $p_1=p_2$; then $\Delta_j\circ p_1$ has components $(p_1,p_1)=(p_1,p_2)$, so $\Delta_j\circ p_1=\mathrm{id}$, and $p_1\circ\Delta_j=\mathrm{id}_U$. An isomorphism is a homeomorphism, so the preimage under $\Delta_j$ of every quasi-compact open is quasi-compact: $\Delta_j$ is quasi-compact and $j$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PE (lemma-extend-trivial), proof, lines 2806-2843 (first paragraph for $j$ separated and quasi-compact and $j_*$ quasi-coherent; part (2) for $\mathcal H=\Ker(\mathcal F\oplus j_*\mathcal G\to j_*j^*\mathcal F)$; part (3) 'with its obvious map to $\mathcal F$ and its obvious identification with $\mathcal G$ over $U$'), first paragraph of the proof (Schemes 01L7)

proof.text: *Step 2 (the modules $j_*\mathcal G$ and $j_*(\mathcal F|_U)$ and the map $d$).* For an $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal M$ let $j_*\mathcal M$ be the direct image [def-pc-module-pullback]: $(j_*\mathcal M)(W)=\mathcal M(W\cap U)$ for $W\subseteq X$ open, with the restriction maps of $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal O_X(W)$ acting through the restriction $\mathcal O_X(W)\to\mathcal O_X(W\cap U)=\mathcal O_U(W\cap U)$; for a morphism $\beta$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules, $(j_*\beta)_W=\beta_{W\cap U}$. The restriction $\mathcal F|_U$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (2), and $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent by hypothesis; by Step 1 and [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] (Schemes 01LC) $j_*\mathcal G$ and $j_*(\mathcal F|_U)$ are quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Let $a:\mathcal F\to j_*(\mathcal F|_U)$, $a_W(f)=f|_{W\cap U}$; it is $\mathcal O_X$-linear because the restriction maps of $\mathcal F$ are semilinear [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and compatible with restrictions. Let $b=j_*\varphi:j_*\mathcal G\to j_*(\mathcal F|_U)$, $b_W(g)=\varphi_{W\cap U}(g)$. On the direct sum $\mathcal F\oplus j_*\mathcal G$ ($W\mapsto\mathcal F(W)\oplus\mathcal G(W\cap U)$), which is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-direct-sum], define the $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $d:\mathcal F\oplus j_*\mathcal G\to j_*(\mathcal F|_U)$, $d_W(f,g)=a_W(f)-b_W(g)=f|_{W\cap U}-\varphi_{W\cap U}(g)$ (this fixes the sign convention of the source's map $\mathcal F\oplus j_*\mathcal G\to j_*j^*\mathcal F$; here $j^*\mathcal F=\mathcal F|_U$).

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PE (lemma-extend-trivial), proof, lines 2806-2843 (first paragraph for $j$ separated and quasi-compact and $j_*$ quasi-coherent; part (2) for $\mathcal H=\Ker(\mathcal F\oplus j_*\mathcal G\to j_*j^*\mathcal F)$; part (3) 'with its obvious map to $\mathcal F$ and its obvious identification with $\mathcal G$ over $U$'), first and second paragraphs (Schemes 01LC, Schemes Section 01LA)

proof.text: *Step 3 ($\mathcal H$ and $\psi$).* Let $\mathcal H=\ker d$, the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal F\oplus j_*\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal H(W)=\{(f,g)\in\mathcal F(W)\oplus\mathcal G(W\cap U):f|_{W\cap U}=\varphi_{W\cap U}(g)\}$ (kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ are sectionwise). Its source and target being quasi-coherent (Step 2), $\mathcal H$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Let $\psi:\mathcal H\to\mathcal F$ be the first projection, $\psi_W(f,g)=f$; it is $\mathcal O_X$-linear and compatible with restrictions, being the composite of the inclusion $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal F\oplus j_*\mathcal G$ with the projection to $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PE (lemma-extend-trivial), proof, lines 2806-2843 (first paragraph for $j$ separated and quasi-compact and $j_*$ quasi-coherent; part (2) for $\mathcal H=\Ker(\mathcal F\oplus j_*\mathcal G\to j_*j^*\mathcal F)$; part (3) 'with its obvious map to $\mathcal F$ and its obvious identification with $\mathcal G$ over $U$'), second paragraph ($\mathcal H$ is quasi-coherent, Schemes Section 01LA) and part (3) ('its obvious map to $\mathcal F$')

proof.text: *Step 4 ($\alpha$ and $\varphi\circ\alpha=\psi|_U$).* By definition of restriction [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], for an open $W\subseteq U$ we have $(\mathcal H|_U)(W)=\mathcal H(W)$, and $W\cap U=W$, so $(\mathcal H|_U)(W)=\{(f,g)\in\mathcal F(W)\oplus\mathcal G(W):f=\varphi_W(g)\}$. Define $\alpha_W:(\mathcal H|_U)(W)\to\mathcal G(W)$, $\alpha_W(f,g)=g$. It is $\mathcal O_U(W)$-linear and commutes with the restriction maps (both are componentwise), so $\alpha:\mathcal H|_U\to\mathcal G$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules; and $g\mapsto(\varphi_W(g),g)$ is an inverse of $\alpha_W$ for every $W$ (it lands in $(\mathcal H|_U)(W)$, and $(f,g)\mapsto g\mapsto(\varphi_W(g),g)=(f,g)$), compatible with restrictions since $\varphi$ is, so $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. Finally, for $W\subseteq U$ and $(f,g)\in(\mathcal H|_U)(W)$: $(\varphi\circ\alpha)_W(f,g)=\varphi_W(g)=f=\psi_W(f,g)=(\psi|_U)_W(f,g)$. Hence $\varphi\circ\alpha=\psi|_U$, and $(\mathcal H,\psi,\alpha)$ has all the required properties.
